local_checks.invariant: Any http:// --base-url reaches only a loopback host, so x-api-key never travels in clear over a network (ask-claude.sh:88-96). The same BASE_URL feeds every curl call: 251 (messages), 381/384 (ma_call), 401 (session stream), 668 (file upload), 698 (file download).
local_checks.result: The gate is a shell glob on the raw string. The patterns http://localhost[:/]*, http://127.0.0.1[:/]* and http://\[::1\][:/]* accept a ':' after the loopback literal, and nothing after it is checked. curl reads 'localhost:' as RFC 3986 userinfo when an '@' follows, so http://localhost:@evil.host passes the gate, and the authority curl connects to is evil.host. No later check of the host exists. No curl call passes -L, and https://* to any host is accepted by design.

local_checks.invariant: A credential meant for one MCP server is delegated only to that server (credential audience narrowing).
local_checks.result: ask-claude.sh:101-103 checks only that each --mcp value starts with https://. At ask-claude.sh:276 the space-joined URL list goes to request.jq. At lib/request.jq:58-59 one env.ASK_CLAUDE_MCP_TOKEN is attached as authorization_token to every mcp_servers entry. No per-server token mapping exists, and nothing warns when the token is set and more than one server is given. The token is read from the environment, not from argv. The README (lines 18 and 33) documents the token as being 'for the --mcp servers', so the fan-out is documented but not scoped.

local_checks.invariant: Bounded replay run with two --mcp servers and one token: inspect the request body.
local_checks.result: The logged request body has mcp_servers equal to [{url:https://a.example/mcp, name:a-example, authorization_token:tok_FOR_SERVER_A_ONLY}, {url:https://b.example/mcp, name:b-example, authorization_token:tok_FOR_SERVER_A_ONLY}]. Server B is bound to server A's token.

local_checks.invariant: MCP server and tool identity binding: two servers must not be able to claim one identity.
local_checks.result: The name comes from host() (lib/request.jq:38): the host before the first '/' or ':', with any character outside [A-Za-z0-9_-] replaced by '-'. As a result, a-b.example and a.b.example collide, and so do two paths on one host. The mcp_toolset refers to its server by that name (line 66). Server-side routing and duplicate-name handling are done by the provider and are not observable locally. The URLs come only from the user, so no attacker can choose the colliding name, and no finding is recorded for this.

local_checks.invariant: A credential meant for one MCP server is delegated only to that server (credential audience narrowing).

No per-server token variable, mapping, or multi-server warning exists. README.md:18 says the token 'is sent as its authorization token' and README.md:33 says it is for 'the --mcp servers'. The hunter's second blocker (product intent) is dropped: it is not a boundary fact an owner can observe, and the documented fan-out does not narrow the audience. Not refuted by source.

local_checks.invariant: The state dir that holds history, the .stream.$$ log and the .always.$$ grant file must be a directory only the invoking user controls before any fixed name in it is trusted or written (ask-claude.sh:113-120).
local_checks.result: The verbatim gate (lines 113-120) passes for a directory owned by uid 0, mode 755, while running as uid 1000: chmod 700 fails, the failure is discarded because there is no set -e and the && result is unchecked, and ls -ldnL | cut -c6,9 inspects only group/other write bits, never the owner and never parent directories. The run used a read-only rootfs dir, so chmod failed with EROFS instead of EPERM; both are discarded the same way.

local_checks.invariant: A fixed-name file in $STATE must not grant authority unless the current process created it.
local_checks.result: session_confirm (ask-claude.sh:434-437) returns allow when $STATE/.always.$$ exists, whatever its owner or creator. A second account that owns $STATE can pre-create .always.<N> for the whole PID range and .stream.<N> files (line 480/484) so that every tool confirmation of the victim's agent session is auto-allowed. This impact is source-only, because the sandbox has a single uid and cannot stage a second owner.

local_checks.invariant: Baseline comparison: does the predecessor bind the state-dir owner?
local_checks.result: docs/claude.sh:47 and 111-112 use the same mkdir/chmod plus a write-bit-only check with no owner check, so the gap is inherited. Its STATE is fixed under $HOME, whereas ask-claude.sh:66 honours XDG_STATE_HOME, which widens where $STATE can resolve.

local_checks.invariant: Trace lines and scopes match source.
local_checks.result: Confirmed: 66 sets STATE from XDG_STATE_HOME/HOME; 54 is set -uo pipefail (no -e); 113 mkdir -p && chmod 700 with status unused; 118-120 test cut -c6,9 of ls -ldnL only; 434-437 return allow on existence of $STATE/.always.$$, before the no-TTY deny at 438-442; 447 creates the grant; 480/484 fixed .stream.$$ log. docs/claude.sh baseline shares the write-bit-only pattern (hunter's check; not re-derived here beyond calibration).

local_checks.invariant: The state-dir gate must refuse a directory the invoking user does not own.
local_checks.result: In the sandbox as uid 1000, the real script with XDG_STATE_HOME=/scratch/stD, where stD/ask-claude is a symlink to /usr/share (uid 0, mode 755), printed the chmod error and then proceeded past the gate to line 484 (session_turn). The gate did not die. Control: an own mode-777 dir was fixed by chmod 700 and proceeded normally. Note chmod failed with EROFS (read-only rootfs) rather than EPERM; both are discarded identically.

local_checks.invariant: A tool confirmation must not be allowed by a file the current run did not create.
local_checks.result: Replay fixtures fx/1.sse (agent.tool_use bash, requires_action) and fx/2.sse (end_turn), stdin </dev/null, ASK_CLAUDE_CONFIRM unset. Control (fresh state dir): 'denied bash ... stdin is not a terminal' and the request log carried result deny. With .always.1..2000 pre-planted in a mode-700 state dir: 'ask-claude: allowed bash ({"command":"echo pwned"})' and the request log carried result allow. This shows a pre-existing grant overrides the no-TTY deny. Single uid, so cross-account ownership was not staged. Sandbox jq 1.7 vs pinned 1.8.2; the fold program ran without error and no version dependence is relevant.

x_hardening: session_files: with --force and $name an existing directory, mv -- "$name.part" "$name" (703) moves the download into that directory instead of replacing it; use mv -T (GNU) or refuse non-regular targets.
session_files: TOCTOU between the -e check (693) and mv (703). A $name created during the download is silently clobbered; mv -n or an exclusive link-based rename would close it.

session_files: the API file id is interpolated into the URL path without -g or validation (698). This stays on the same host with no -L, so it is not SSRF; validating ^file_[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$ removes path-normalisation surprises.

State dir: .stream.$$ (480) and .always.$$ (447) are fixed, PID-predictable names created with : > (no O_EXCL). Safe only while the owner gap above is closed; a mktemp-based name would not depend on the gate.

local_checks.invariant: An 'always' answer at the confirmation prompt grants only the process that received it (comment ask-claude.sh:422-425); no later process may inherit it.
local_checks.result: The grant is a file $STATE/.always.$$ created at ask-claude.sh:447 and tested only by existence at :434. Nothing removes it: session_cleanup (:556-561) deletes only the stream log, there is no EXIT trap, and no code clears a stale file at startup. Any later ask-claude process whose PID equals a past granting PID skips the prompt, and the grant check (:434) runs before the no-TTY deny (:438), so the stale grant also overrides the unattended default deny.

local_checks.invariant: A new process with no user answer must not send result=allow for an agent.tool_use confirmation.
local_checks.result: Two separate sandbox containers (deterministic PID 12 for the script). Invocation A: user typed 'a' on a pty; .always.12 remained in the state dir after exit. Invocation B: new process, empty stdin (no answer typed), ASK_CLAUDE_CONFIRM unset: no prompt was printed and the client POSTed {"type":"user.tool_confirmation","tool_use_id":"sevt_T1","result":"allow"}.

local_checks.invariant: Confirmation rounds stop or remain user-gated; custom-tool rounds capped at 8.
local_checks.result: rounds increments only when asks is empty (:528), so confirmation rounds are uncapped; each still needs a user answer unless ASK_CLAUDE_CONFIRM=allow or an always grant applies. Spend is the user's own and server-side budget (session-create.jq:37) is the cap. Recorded as hardening, not a finding.

local_checks.invariant: An 'always' grant must not outlive the process that received it, and a new process with no answer must not send result=allow.
local_checks.result: Confirmed. The grant file is written at :447 and checked by existence at :434, before the no-TTY deny at :438. `rg '\.always'` across the repository finds only those two lines. session_cleanup (:556-561) removes only the stream log and resets only the INT trap. The script has no EXIT trap. session_prereqs (:745-770), which runs before `agent` (:775) and `agent resume` (:819), clears nothing. $$ inside the session_confirm command substitution is the parent script's PID, so the key is per script process. The proposed fix in session_prereqs covers both entry forms and is not clobbered by `trap - INT`.

local_checks.invariant: A new process with no user answer must send result=deny for an agent.tool_use confirmation.
local_checks.result: Violated. Container 1, process A under script(1), answer 'a': left .always.15. New container, process B, same launch shape (PID 15), empty stdin: no prompt, result=allow sent. Control with a fresh state dir: prompt shown, result=deny. Runs with a different PID: deny, which shows the grant is bound only by PID equality. No pty, stdin /dev/null, matching stale grant (PID 13): result=allow, overriding the unattended default deny. Run with sandbox-run.sh (no network, read-only target, dummy key, replay fixtures). local_checks.result: bump-effver:30-37 reads VERSION from the working copy and evaluates $((x+1)), $((y+1)), $((z+1)) with no version_re check, so the same arithmetic-subscript injection proven for check-effver applies. But here VERSION comes from the checked-out working copy, whose writer can equally edit bump-effver, effver.just and justfile that the user is executing: same trust as the code being run, no boundary crossed. A merged hostile VERSION would also have failed check-effver's version_re on the current commit (check-effver:85). effver.just:7 interpolates $(cat VERSION) into a sed replacement only after bump-effver wrote a computed numeric version. `effort` is restricted by the case at bump-effver:15-21; `date` (argv 2) goes only into the awk -v heading text. Covered; hardening note filed.

local_checks.result: version_re (85) is applied only to the current commit's VERSION, and a mismatch only appends to problems[] without skipping later commits. The parent VERSION read at 71-75 goes into $old unvalidated, then bump "$old" "$effort" (103) evaluates $((y + 1)) / $((z + 1)) / $((x + 1)) (56-60). The bash arithmetic evaluator expands an array subscript in a variable's value, including $(...).

local_checks.result: Sandbox (bash 5.2.21, git 2.51.1, no network): fixture repo base(0.4.0) -> parent(VERSION `0.4.x[$(touch /scratch/PWNED_check_effver)]`) -> child(0.4.1, valid micro heading). `bash /target/tools/effver/check-effver main~2..main` reported the parent's bad VERSION, then created /scratch/PWNED_check_effver while it checked the child; exit 1. A first attempt with subscript base `a` aborted on `set -u` (a: unbound variable) before the subscript expanded, so the payload needs a set array name (x, y, z or BASH_VERSINFO).
